key_insight: The paper shows that 3D Gaussian Splatting becomes unreliable in regions that were never seen during training, and it introduces a visibility-aware uncertainty field to identify and handle those areas. By modeling anisotropic visibility, the method helps active mapping focus on the most informative next viewpoints.
problem_solved: 3D Gaussian Splatting can make overly confident or inaccurate predictions in unseen regions, which limits its reliability for reconstruction and exploration. This work addresses how to quantify uncertainty in 3DGS and use it to guide active mapping.
method: Define an anisotropic visibility field for each Gaussian particle relative to the training views.
Represent visibility efficiently with spherical harmonics to make uncertainty estimation practical for 3DGS.
Use the resulting uncertainty signal to support active mapping and select better next viewpoints.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this improves the trustworthiness of 3D reconstruction from sparse views and enables smarter exploration strategies. It is especially useful for robotics, 3D perception, and autonomous mapping systems that need to know where their models are uncertain.

paper_title: Uncertainty-driven 3D Gaussian Splatting Active Mapping via Anisotropic Visibility Field
paper_authors: Shangjie Xue, Jesse Dill, Dhruv Ahuja, Frank Dellaert, Panagiotis Tsiotras
